observations.quote: The world was the first figure or image of God, Man is the image of the World
observations.note: Opens a chain of images running downward: God, world, Man, Animall, Zoophite, Plant, Mettalls, stones.

observations.quote: the Zoophite or sensible hearb is the image of the Animall
observations.note: Zoophite is glossed sensible hearb, a rank set between the Animall and the Plant.

observations.quote: The great world is in every thing one with the little world, as the child with its parent
observations.note: Great world and little world are one in every thing; the likeness given is child and parent.

observations.quote: the prudent Ancients wilsely called Man a Microcosm or little World
observations.name: Ancients
observations.note: The name Microcosm for Man is given to the Ancients, and the author approves it.

observations.quote: a Microcosm or little World, which few now a dayes understand, that the great visible World was made Man
observations.note: Stated: the sense of the name is that the great visible World was made Man; the text says few now understand it, not that it is kept back.

observations.quote: so also the little world man is twofold, visible in respect of his Body, invisible in respect of his Spirit
observations.what: the little world man is twofold
observations.note: Man is twofold as the great world is bipartite: visible Body, invisible Spirit.

observations.quote: one a syderiall Spirit from the Firmament, the other from the breath of life
observations.note: Two Spirits in Man are set apart by their sources: the Firmament and the breath of life.

observations.quote: the other from the breath of life, which is the Intellectuall Soul inspired from God, and the mouth of the most High
observations.note: The second Spirit, from the breath of life, is said to be the Intellectuall Soul inspired from God.

observations.quote: Man hath three parts, a mortall Body with a Syderiall Spirit, and an immortall Soule
observations.note: Right after the twofold and two-Spirit divisions, Man is counted in three parts; the Syderiall Spirit goes with the mortall Body.

observations.quote: an immortall Soule, which is the cottage of the Image of God or of the holy Spirit in Man
observations.note: The immortall Soule is called the cottage of the Image of God or of the holy Spirit in Man.

observations.quote: The first Spirit is from the Limbus or greater world; the second from the word Fiat.
observations.note: The margin glosses Limbus as the greater world and gives the second Spirit's source as the word Fiat.

observations.quote: Angelicall according to which he is to live, and Animall which is not to be regarded
observations.note: The margin names two wisdoms in Man, Angelicall to live by and Animall not to be regarded; a one-letter gap stands earlier in the note.

observations.quote: Regeneration overcometh a bad birth.
observations.note: The margin says Regeneration overcomes a bad birth; the lines given do not say more of it.

observations.quote: If a man live sensually by his own proper and proud Will according to flesh and blood onely, he is but a Brute or Beast
observations.note: First of three ways of living: sensually, by which a man is but a Brute or Beast.

observations.quote: (according to those Epithites in Scripture) he be a Dog, Fox, Wolfe, Sheep, Sow, or generation of Vipers
observations.name: Scripture
observations.note: The beast names for the sensual man are given as Scripture's Epithites.

observations.quote: of which I shall discourse more at large in my Treatise of Signatures
observations.note: The author points to his own Treatise of Signatures and forbears to speak more of it here, giving that treatise as the reason.

observations.quote: If he live Rationally, then he is a Man
observations.note: Second way of living: Rationally, by which he is a Man.

observations.quote: and hath dominion over the living Creatures in his body
observations.note: The rational man has dominion over the living Creatures in his body. Interpreted: the phrase points to creatures said to be inside man; the lines given do not say what they are.

observations.quote: The invisible or immortall body of Man from the breath of God is not subject to Stars or Astronomers.
observations.note: The margin exempts the invisible or immortall body from the breath of God from Stars and Astronomers.

observations.quote: The invisible or immortall body of Man from the breath of God is not subject to Stars or Astronomers.
observations.note: N103 calls the invisible body immortall, from the breath of God, and free of the Stars; MICRO.17 has the invisible body from the Firmament, MICRO.24 makes the invisible Body of Reason and an Astrall Spirit, and MICRO.27 calls that Spirit mortall and ruled by the Astra's.

observations.quote: then hath he dominion over the Stars and all things else
observations.note: Third way of living: according to the God-like Spirit, upon the Tree of Life; it gives dominion over the Stars and all things else.

observations.quote: if (I say) he live according to the Talent and Treasure laid up in his Earthen Vessell and committed to him
observations.note: With (I say) the author restates living upon the Tree of Life in other figures: Talent, Treasure, Earthen Vessell. The lines given do not say plainly what the Treasure is.

observations.quote: Man comprehends and carryeth all things about in himselfe; whereof he is made that beareth he in himselfe
observations.note: Man carries all things in himself because he bears what he is made of.

observations.quote: He was made of the world, he beareth the world about in him, and is borne of the world.
observations.note: Three relations of Man to the world: made of it, bearing it, borne of it.

observations.quote: the first matter (which was a kind of ineffigiate confused Essence, which Phylosophers call the Chaos and Hylen, or Mother of the world) was the seed of the great world
observations.note: The first matter is said to be a kind of ineffigiate confused Essence and the seed of the great world.

observations.quote: which Phylosophers call the Chaos and Hylen, or Mother of the world
observations.name: Phylosophers
observations.note: The names Chaos, Hylen and Mother of the world for the first matter are given to the Phylosophers.

observations.quote: was the seed of the great world, so the great world is the seed of Adam or Man
observations.note: As the first matter is seed of the great world, so the great world is seed of Adam or Man.

observations.quote: so Man (Adam) lay hid in the world
observations.note: Man lay hid in the world as the world in the invisible Waters: a hiding of one thing in another, contained before brought forth, not of a teaching.

observations.quote: The first matter was made a world, and the great World was made Man.
observations.note: Two makings in a row: first matter into a world, the great World into Man.

observations.quote: As a Tree groweth from the seed, the seed is the beginning of the Tree, and the seed also is the end of the Tree
observations.note: The likeness of Tree and seed: the seed is both beginning and end of the Tree.

observations.quote: for in every graine or seed of the Tree there lies hid another Tree
observations.note: Another Tree lies hid in every seed; again a hiding of thing in thing.

observations.quote: which Paracelsus calleth the Limbus, whose Earth was the WORD of the Lord
observations.name: Paracelsus
observations.note: Limbus is given as Paracelsus' name for the First Matter, the seed of all things to be created; its Earth is said to be the WORD of the Lord.

observations.quote: which Paracelsus calleth the Limbus
observations.note: Here the Limbus is the First Matter, the seed which was made a world; N101 has the Limbus or greater world, as one thing.

observations.quote: and Man was the last of all as the perfect seed, which againe is able out of himselfe to beget another Man like himself
observations.note: Man is the last created and the perfect seed, able to beget another Man like himself.

observations.quote: And though Man be not a seed as other seed is, yet hath he power to cast seed out of himselfe
observations.note: Stated: the text itself says Man is not a seed as other seed is, so seed said of Man is used in a second sense.

observations.quote: so every one that is borne of him bears about him that which he did, viz. the whole world
observations.note: Every one born of Adam bears the whole world as Adam did.

observations.quote: all men are but one man, of flesh, blood, and spirit
observations.note: All men are said to be one man.

observations.quote: Therefore the knowledge of Man is to be taken from both Lights, as the Son cannot be known from himselfe alone but from his Father
observations.note: Man is known from both Lights, as a Son from his Father; this sentence does not name the two Lights, while MICRO.21 names the Light of Nature.

observations.quote: Man hath two Fathers, an Eternall whose Image he beareth, and a Mortall one, which is the whole world with all the creatures
observations.note: Man's two Fathers: an Eternall one, and a Mortall one which is the whole world.

observations.quote: that is, that Limus Terrae, that slime of the earth, or hidden Secret thing
observations.note: Limus Terrae is glossed slime of the earth and set equal, by that is, to the mortal Father, the whole world with all the creatures.

observations.quote: that slime of the earth, or hidden Secret thing
observations.note: The Limus Terrae is called a hidden Secret thing.

observations.quote: the most precious Esse or Being of all creatures, which all Phylosophers, Physitians Astronomers, and Divines are to consider and diligently inquire into
observations.note: The same thing is called the most precious Esse or Being of all creatures, and four kinds of learned men are told to inquire into it.

observations.quote: In the lesser world Man there is no member or part that doth not answer to some Element, some Planet, some Intelligence or other
observations.note: Every member or part of Man answers to some Element, Planet or Intelligence.

observations.quote: to some measure and number in the Archetype or first pattern
observations.note: Archetype is glossed first pattern.

observations.quote: Man hath a visible body from the Elements as a fit garment and sutable cottage for the Soul
observations.note: The visible body is from the Elements and is garment and cottage for the Soul.

observations.quote: Aetheriall and Astrall Body or chariot and vehicle of the Soule, wherein the Intellectuall Soul and earthy Body like two Extreams are knit, glued and confederate together
observations.what: chariot and vehicle of the Soule
observations.note: The invisible body from the Heaven or Firmament is called chariot and vehicle of the Soule and joins Soul and earthy Body as two Extreams.

observations.quote: in this third mean which partaketh of the other two they are coupled and united into one intire man
observations.note: The astral body is a third mean partaking of the other two, in which they are united into one man.

observations.quote: Water is the Matrix of the world, upon which the Spirit of God moved, Gen. 1.
observations.name: Gen. 1
observations.note: The margin calls Water the Matrix of the world and names Gen. 1 beside the passage on the world hid in the invisible Waters.

observations.quote: The Earth plung'd or swam up out of the Water, 2 Pet. 3.5.
observations.name: 2 Pet. 3.5
observations.note: The margin names 2 Pet. 3.5 for the Earth coming up out of the Water.

observations.quote: so God extracted every creature out of the first matter
observations.note: The margin likens creation to a craftsman's many shapes: God extracted every creature out of the first matter. A one-letter gap stands earlier in the note.

observations.quote: that Earth or field which hath all seeds in it self
observations.note: The margin calls Man the Earth or field that has all seeds in itself; a one-letter gap stands just before these words.

observations.quote: As the Son is not lesser then his Father, so Man is not lesser then the World.
observations.note: The margin says Man is not lesser than the World, as the Son than his Father.

observations.quote: None can know the image unlesse he first know him whose image he is.
observations.note: A rule of knowing: the image is known only through him whose image it is.

observations.quote: Hermes calleth Man an earthly God.
observations.name: Hermes
observations.note: The name earthly God for Man is given to Hermes.

observations.name: Gen. 2.7
observations.note: The margin names Gen. 2.7 beside the passage on the Limus Terrae, the slime of the earth.

observations.quote: The perfection and dignity of Man.
observations.what: The perfection and dignity of Man
observations.note: A margin heading set beside the passage on the third, astral body.

observations.quote: Through this Medium, this middle Aetheriall little body
observations.note: Medium is here the middle Aetheriall little body.

observations.quote: by the command of God, who is the Centre of the great world, and by the imploying of his Intelligences or Spirits to that end
observations.note: God is called the Centre of the great world; the Soule's descent is by his command and his Intelligences or Spirits.

observations.quote: is first poured and descendeth into the middle poynt of the Heart, which is the Centre of the little world
observations.note: Through the Aetheriall body the Intellectuall Soule descends first into the Heart, called the Centre of the little world.

observations.quote: by which heat it joyneth to the Spirit begotten from the heart, by the spirit it drencheth it selfe into the blood, by the blood it cleaveth to all the members
observations.note: The order of joining: vehicle, naturall heat, Spirit of the heart, blood, members.

observations.quote: whose operations it draweth to it selfe by a peculiar magnetick vertue, just as the visible body doth the efficacy of the Elements
observations.note: The Aethereall body keeps the course of the Firmament and draws its operations by a magnetick vertue, as the visible body draws the Elements'.

observations.quote: and so remaineth one (thing) with the visible and invisible world
observations.note: The Aethereall body remains one with the visible and invisible world; the word thing stands in brackets in the text.

observations.quote: The whole Firmament is in us with the Planets and Stars
observations.note: The whole Firmament with Planets and Stars is said to be in us.

observations.quote: so that of the syderiall spirit of the Firmament we may learn all Naturall things
observations.note: The Stars pierce into Man; from the syderiall spirit all Naturall things may be learned.

observations.quote: Thus God and Man cannot be united but by a Mean, even our Saviour who partaketh of two Natures
observations.note: The margin sets a likeness beside the Medium of soul and body: God and Man are united only by a Mean, our Saviour of two Natures.

observations.quote: is infused by God into the Elementary body through the Astra's as a Medium
observations.name: Paracelsus
observations.note: That the soul is infused into the Elementary body through the Astra's as a Medium is given as Paracelsus' saying; two one-letter gaps stand just before these words.

observations.quote: John 10.30.
observations.name: John 10.30
observations.note: The margin names John 10.30 where the text says one with the world as the Son with his Father.

observations.quote: The MIND.
observations.note: A margin heading set at the end of MICRO.18, after the sentence on learning all Naturall things from the syderiall spirit and before the paragraph on the Intellectuall and immortal Soul.

observations.quote: with the four foresaid inhabitants of the Elements, which the bruit beasts have not
observations.note: The word foresaid points back to an earlier place in this writing; the lines given do not include it.

observations.quote: or Spirit by the inbreathing of God, created
observations.note: The Intellectuall and immortal Soul or Spirit is by God's inbreathing, created after the Image of God and the Divine Triunity.

observations.quote: that so in all things he might be one with his Heavenly Father, who is in us by his Spirit
observations.note: The end named for this creation: that Man be one with his Heavenly Father, who is in us by his Spirit.

observations.quote: from which we learn sacred Divinity and all heavenly and earthly secrets without errour
observations.note: From the Father's Spirit in us all heavenly and earthly secrets are learned without errour; the text speaks of secrets learned, not of hiding them.

observations.name: Zach. 12.1. Gen. 2.7. Es. 42.5. Wisd. 2.23.
observations.note: The margin names four places of Scripture beside the Intellectuall and immortal Soul made by God's inbreathing.

observations.quote: 1 John 2.27. Chap. 4.14. Acts 17.28.
observations.name: 1 John 2.27. Chap. 4.14. Acts 17.28.
observations.note: The margin names these places beside the sentence that ends: in him we are, and live, and are moved.

observations.quote: As God is One in Essence, Trine (or Three) in persons, so Man is One in Person, Trine (or Three) in distinct Essence
observations.note: God and Man in mirrored order: one Essence and three persons; one Person and three Essences.

observations.quote: composed Triune, of a Terrene Body, an Aethereall Spirit of the Heavens, and a living vivifying Soule which God breathed into him, and is the house of God
observations.note: Stated: what Triune means of Man: Terrene Body, Aethereall Spirit, and the Soule God breathed in, which is the house of God.

observations.quote: This the holy Scripture witnesseth
observations.name: holy Scripture
observations.note: The author calls the holy Scripture as witness to Man's threefold make; no words of it are given here.

observations.quote: Unitrine or Triune, One in Three, or Three in One
observations.note: Unitrine or Triune is glossed One in Three, or Three in One.

observations.quote: the unanimous consent of all that truly professed Phylosophy from the Light of Nature
observations.name: all that truly professed Phylosophy
observations.note: A second witness beside Scripture: the consent of all who truly professed Phylosophy from the Light of Nature; no words of theirs are given.

observations.name: Luke 1.47; 1 Thes. 5.23; Gen. 2.7
observations.note: The margin names the places of Scripture meant by the witness.

observations.quote: of Rhunrad worthy of perpetuall memory
observations.name: Rhunrad
observations.note: The margin sends the reader to a writing of Rhunrad and praises it; its title has a one-letter gap.

observations.quote: Paul the greatest Phylosopher and Divine shewes three parts of Man, Spirit, Soule and Body.
observations.name: Paul
observations.note: The three parts are given to Paul, called the greatest Phylosopher and Divine, in the order Spirit, Soule and Body.

observations.quote: There are two Souls or two Spirits in Man, Mortall from the first matter which is the life of the body, and Immortall from God.
observations.note: The margin gives the mortal Spirit from the first matter; MICRO.14 gives the syderiall Spirit from the Firmament, and N101 the first Spirit from the Limbus or greater world.

observations.quote: The Spirit is the Life of the Soule, the Spirit and Soule are the life of the body.
observations.note: An order of life among the three: Spirit to Soule, Spirit and Soule to body; John 14 is named beside it.

observations.quote: If happily there should be any that deny these three parts
observations.note: The author supposes deniers of the three parts and answers them with what they must still acknowledge; no words of theirs are given.

observations.quote: Man was created è Limo Terrae, out of the clay or dust of the Earth, by the word FIAT
observations.note: è Limo Terrae is glossed out of the clay or dust of the Earth; MICRO.17 glosses Limus Terrae slime of the earth.

observations.quote: which is that Linum Caelorum, or slime of the Heavens from the Lord
observations.note: The eternall Spirit or breath of life is named Linum Caelorum, glossed slime of the Heavens.

observations.quote: The Limus Terrae, or dust of the Earth, is two-fold, visible and invisible
observations.note: The Limus Terrae is said to be two-fold, visible and invisible.

observations.quote: He hath his Body or cottage from the Earth and Water; but the life that dwells therein is from the Aire and Firmament of Fire
observations.note: The four are divided: Body from Earth and Water, life from Aire and Firmament of Fire.

observations.quote: which life is the Syderiall Spirit, and is properly the Man, not flesh and blood
observations.note: Stated: the Syderiall Spirit is the life dwelling in the body, and is properly the Man, not flesh and blood.

observations.quote: As the Syderiall Spirit is the life of the Body, so the Spirit of the Lord is the life of the Intellectuall Soule.
observations.note: A proportion: Syderiall Spirit to Body as Spirit of the Lord to Intellectuall Soule.

observations.quote: as the Sydereall Spirit dwells in the Body and works therein day and night, for this invisible is himselfe the Firmament
observations.note: The Sydereall Spirit works in the Body day and night, is itself the Firmament and has all things in it.

observations.quote: so the Spirit of the Lord, the WORD of God, the eternall man dwells in the Soule
observations.note: Here the Spirit of the Lord dwelling in the Soule is called the eternall man; MICRO.23 says the Syderiall Spirit is properly the Man.

observations.quote: the house is the habitation of the Soule, the Soule is the habitation and cottage of God
observations.note: A ladder of dwellings: the house for the Soule, the Soule for God.

observations.quote: the most compleat figure of the world, and expresse image of God, in whom he rested from creating
observations.note: Man is the most complete figure of the world and express image of God, in whom God rested from creating.

observations.quote: when (I say) he was on the sixt day made up of all things, the last of the Creatures, and image not onely of the eternall God, but also of the great world
observations.note: Man was made on the sixt day, of all things, last, and as image both of God and of the great world.

observations.quote: it followeth that there are three worlds or Heavens in Man
observations.what: three worlds or Heavens in Man
observations.note: The conclusion drawn: three worlds or Heavens in Man; he is all the world and Pattern of the whole Universe.

observations.quote: And therefore some have called him the Fourth World
observations.name: some
observations.note: The name Fourth World for Man, in whom are found all things of the other three, is given to unnamed others.

observations.quote: for which cause also he may be called by the name of every Creature
observations.note: Because all is found in him, Man may bear the name of every Creature; MICRO.15 names beasts he is known by.

observations.quote: for what else is the Spirit of Man which God breathed into him but God himselfe dwelling in us?
observations.note: The Spirit or Mind of Man which God breathed in is said to be God himself dwelling in us.

observations.quote: The invisible Body or true Internall Man consisting of Reason and an Astrall Spirit, agreeth with the Angells, and is their fellow
observations.note: Stated: the invisible Body or true Internall Man consists of Reason and an Astrall Spirit, and is fellow of the Angells.

observations.quote: And if he be a true Magician, he is not inferiour to the Angells in all Magicall operation, and is Lord and Possessor of all things.
observations.note: On a condition, being a true Magician, Man equals the Angells in Magicall operation and is Lord of all things; the lines given do not say what a true Magician is.

observations.quote: His mortall Phisicall Body he hath from the frame of the world and all things created therein, for all Externall things are nothing else but the Body of Man.
observations.note: The mortal body is from the frame of the world; all Externall things are called the Body of Man.

observations.quote: So that he partaketh of a threefold world, of the Archetype or God-like world in God, of the Intellible or Angellicall, of the sensible Elementall or corporall world
observations.note: The three worlds Man partakes of are named: Archetype, Angellicall, Elementall.

observations.quote: hath a symbolicall operation and conversation with them all
observations.note: Man's operation and conversation with the three worlds is called symbolicall; the lines given do not explain the word.

observations.quote: So that he partaketh of a threefold world
observations.note: Here the worlds are counted three; the numbered heads that follow run from 1 to 5, with Firmament and Stars, Elements, and Elemented things as separate heads.

observations.quote: God created Man to be his Tabernacle as well in this as in the world to come.
observations.note: The margin says Man was created to be God's Tabernacle in this world and the next.

observations.quote: Exemplumque Dei quisque est in imagine parvâ, Manilus.
observations.name: Manilus
observations.note: A Latin line is given under the name Manilus beside Man as Pattern of the Universe; the note does not English it.

observations.quote: That which is Naturated savoureth of the Nature of that which did Naturate it.
observations.note: A margin rule: the thing Naturated savours of what Naturated it.

observations.quote: God dwelleth in the Soul as in the Heaven of Man.
observations.note: The margin calls the Soul the Heaven of Man, where God dwells.

observations.quote: He communicateth with God in his Soule or Mind, because by the breath of life he was made after his image
observations.note: First of five numbered heads (MICRO.25 to MICRO.29), each naming something Man shares in: here God, through Soule or Mind.

observations.quote: the Intellectuall Soul is a certaine particle of the Divine Soule
observations.note: Stated: the Intellectuall Soul is a particle of the Divine Soule.

observations.quote: God hath sowen certaine seeds and resemblances of his Mind in us, much like to that of an Eccho
observations.note: God has sown seeds and resemblances of his Mind in the Soule; the likeness given is an Eccho.

observations.quote: The mind raised up into the most High God and united with him converseth with God, and doth the same works
observations.note: The mind raised and united with God converses with him and does the same works.

observations.quote: neither is there any thing in God which very thing is not represented in Man
observations.note: Every thing in God is said to be represented in Man.

observations.quote: Stern-man of the Soul or Rationall Spirit, & like the eternall God concludeth all Beings, Times and Places
observations.note: The margin says what the Mind is: driver or Stern-man of the Soul or Rationall Spirit; a gap of foreign script follows the word Mind, and a one-letter gap stands before these words.

observations.quote: He hath a semblance with the Angells in respect of the invisible Body and Rationall Soul
observations.note: Second head: likeness with the Angells by the invisible Body and Rationall Soul, with the same wisdome they have.

observations.quote: for he is Gabalis socius Angelorum, a curdled companion of the Angells, or one mixed with in fellowship
observations.note: A Latin name for Man is Englished two ways: a curdled companion of the Angells, or one mixed with in fellowship.

observations.quote: He participateth with the Firmament and Stars of whom he received that Astrall body or Syderiall Spirit, which is the true Astrall Man
observations.note: Third head: Astrall body and Syderiall Spirit, named as one, are received from Firmament and Stars and called the true Astrall Man.

observations.quote: for flesh and blood is not the Man, but the Spirit contained in them
observations.note: The Man is the Spirit contained in flesh and blood, not flesh and blood; MICRO.23 says the same.

observations.quote: which Astrall Spirit is the subject of humane Reason that containeth the sences and wisdome in it
observations.note: Stated: the Astrall Spirit is the subject of humane Reason and holds the sences and wisdome.

observations.quote: and is made (Animall) a living creature with the body
observations.note: The word Animall stands in brackets beside its Englishing, a living creature: the text marks the sense in which the word is used.

observations.quote: This Spirit and the Astra's are but one thing in Man, but the body is the subject of this Spirit
observations.note: The Astrall Spirit and the Astra's are one thing in Man; the body is its subject.

observations.quote: the Astra's rule man in the Spirit, and the Spirit of a man ruleth the Body in flesh and blood
observations.note: An order of rule: Astra's over the Spirit, Spirit over the Body. MICRO.16 gives dominion over the Stars to the one who lives by the God-like Spirit.

observations.quote: This Spirit is mortall; onely the Intellectuall Soule which God breathed into man is immortall.
observations.note: The Astrall Spirit is mortal; only the Intellectuall Soule is immortal.

observations.quote: He partaketh of the Elements, for from these he had his mortall Physicall Earthy body
observations.note: Fourth head: the mortal body is from the Elements.

observations.quote: the world, which is the Parant of Man according to Paracelsus
observations.name: Paracelsus
observations.note: That the world is the Parant of Man is given as according to Paracelsus.

observations.quote: hath in it the four Elementary Spirits of the four inhabitants of the world, as also the fift kind of Flages of a thousand sorts
observations.note: Five kinds of Spirits are counted: four Elementary Spirits of the four inhabitants and a fifth kind, Flages; the lines given do not say what Flages are.

observations.quote: the Imagination also of these five Spirits in the Elements must be in the Microcosm Man
observations.note: The Imagination of the five Spirits must be in Man.

observations.quote: the use of Mans Reason according to the will and command of God, is as a Chaine were with those five Spirits are knit and bound together
observations.note: Reason used by God's will is likened to a Chaine binding the five Spirits so that they acquiesce with Man's Imagination.

observations.quote: He partaketh of all Elemented Animalls, Vegetables and Mineralls
observations.note: Fifth head: Man has in him the Nature and properties of Animalls, Vegetables and Mineralls.

observations.quote: All things were made of nothing and Man was made of all those things.
observations.note: The margin: all things from nothing, Man from all things.

observations.quote: All things were made of nothing
observations.note: This note says all things were made of nothing; MICRO.17 makes the First Matter the seed of all things to be created, and N105 says God extracted every creature out of the first matter.

observations.quote: The great world was the matrix of Adam, thus the whole frame of the world is the mother of all things that are brought forth.
observations.note: The great world is the matrix of Adam; N104 calls Water the Matrix of the world.

observations.quote: Man therefore who was the last is the most excellent and noble of all Creatures, because he hath the parts of the whole world
observations.note: The conclusion of the five heads: Man, the last, is the most excellent creature because he has the parts of the whole world.

observations.quote: nor is there any thing in the great world which may not really be found in man
observations.note: Every thing of the great world is said to be really found in man; the weight lies on the word really.

observations.quote: The Son is like the father in all things, the father being known the Son is known also.
observations.note: The rule of Son and father is repeated: knowing the father gives knowledge of the Son.

observations.quote: most admirable Extract & kernell of the four Elements
observations.what: Extract & kernell of the four Elements
observations.note: Man, the greatest miracle of Nature, is called Extract and kernell of the four Elements.

observations.quote: is truly every Creature, for he is all the world
observations.note: Man is truly every Creature, being all the world.

observations.quote: he alone hath this honor to have semblance with all things, and operation with all, and conuersation with all
observations.note: Man alone has semblance, operation and conversation with all things.

observations.quote: Yea he riseth to such perfection that he is made the Son of God, transformed into the same image which is God and made one with him
observations.note: The highest step named: Man made the Son of God, transformed into the image which is God, one with him.

observations.quote: which is not granted either to Angells, or the world, or any other Creature, but to Man only
observations.note: This union with God is granted to Man only, not to Angells, the world or any other Creature.

observations.name: John 17.11, 12.22, 23
observations.note: The margin names places in John beside Man made one with God.

dropped.reason: The two-word heading N111 stands at the end of MICRO.18, before the paragraph on the Intellectuall Soul; the text does not show it is said of the syderiall spirit, so no clash is shown.
